text:
sam_devex: Heads up — we got a support ticket where a user saw duplicate side-effects during onboarding when the SDK retried a batched request after a 429. They called our /batch/create-items endpoint, got a 200 for some items then a 429 for the batch; SDK retried and ended up creating overlapping items. Anyone seen this pattern?

olga_support: Ugh. Customer says they were using the node SDK default retry behavior, not setting idempotency keys. They quoted our quickstart sampleapp.

marina_platform: Yikes. Is the 200/429 split coming back in one HTTP response, or was it partial at the app layer (some items processed, then rate limit triggered)?

olga_support: The backend returned 200 for the request but the response body had per-item statuses — some items failed with 429 and we treated the whole call as success. SDK then retried the failed items later, which created duplicates for the ones that previously succeeded due to eventual reprocessing.

josh_sdk: Hmm. This is an edge of batched APIs + retry semantics. Our SDK-level retry is keyed to HTTP status codes by default (>=500 and 429). If the API masks per-item failures in the body, SDK can't infer which part to replay.

kevin_api: We need to make the contract clearer. For batch endpoints, the API should return explicit per-item status and an idempotency-safe response code. We can also add a top-level 'retriable' flag.

sam_devex: For the short-term, should we update the sampleapp to recommend per-request idempotency keys or per-item ids? The user was using auto-generated client IDs.

marina_platform: Recommend both. Per-batch Idempotency-Key for whole logical operation, plus item-level client_ids. If the SDK sees a 429 it should surface the per-item statuses to the caller instead of blindly retrying the whole batch.

josh_sdk: Agree. For SDK parity, node/python/go all behave identically today (they retry whole request on 429). We need an opt-in behavior: "safeReplay: true" that will cause the SDK to only retry items explicitly marked retriable in the response.

priya_sre: Also protect users from accidental infinite replay: add an exponential backoff with full jitter + cap and a dedupe window on the client side. Something like:
```
sleep = min(max_backoff, base * 2**attempt) * random()
// base=100ms, max_backoff=30s
```

josh_sdk: Nice. We'll prototype an option in the node SDK called safeBatchReplay and expose hooks for parsing per-item results. Default remains current behaviour to avoid surprises.

kevin_api: We'll push an API change: include an array of 'item_statuses' with fields {item_id, status, retriable: bool, server_op_id:?}. server_op_id is optional but helps reconciliation. We'll also add guidance to the API docs.

olga_support: Can we also update the quickstart sampleapp to show best-practice: set 'Idempotency-Key' header and include client_item_ids in payload? A tiny snippet would help. Customers copy quickstarts.

sam_devex: Yes — quickstart patch should be tiny. Example suggestion in sampleapp: 
```http
POST /batch/create-items
Idempotency-Key: 5f2a...-uuid
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "items": [
    {"client_item_id": "c1", "payload": {...}},
    {"client_item_id": "c2", "payload": {...}}
  ]
}
```

josh_sdk: I'll add safeBatchReplay to node + python with an opt-in flag and a handler that emits metrics when we detect mixed per-item statuses. That should help telemetry.

priya_sre: From ops, add a server-side dedupe window for server_op_id to avoid duplicate application of the same operation if we get retries within X minutes.

ci-bot: deploy queued: docs/update-batch-idempotency-guidance -> staging

marina_platform: Action items: API: add item_statuses + retriable flag (kevin). SDK: implement safeBatchReplay opt-in and sampleapp update (josh). Docs: quickstart snippet + guidance (sam). Support: reach out to affected customer with workaround (olga). SRE: propose server_op_id dedupe (priya).

olga_support: I'll ping the customer and recommend using a per-batch Idempotency-Key and client_item_ids as a workaround until SDK opt-in lands.

sam_devex: Thanks everyone. Let's follow up in this thread with PR links. If anyone needs me to spin the change into a short RFC I can do that tomorrow. :thumbsup:
